utterances.text: Thanks for coming in, Mr. Halloran. Can I get you something to drink?
I'm fine. What's this about? Am I in some kind of trouble?
That depends on the conversation. You know the high school off Cedar?
Sure, everybody does. Look, I already told the guy at the front desk, I don't even know why I'm here.
Just routine. There was some damage done over the weekend. Walk me through Friday night.
Friday I was mostly at my cousin's place. We watched a game, ordered food. Nothing exciting.
And you stayed there the whole night?
Pretty much. I mean, I ran out for a bit because we needed stuff, but I came right back.
What kind of stuff?
Snacks, soda. And I had to grab a can of blue spray paint for my cousin's project, he's doing this poster thing for his shop class.
A can of spray paint. Where'd you buy that?
The hardware place on Fifth. Paid cash, I think. Why, is that a problem?
Not necessarily. Did you end up anywhere near the school that night?
Not really. Well — I cut through the lot behind the school because the light's better, but I didn't stop. I went past the east gymnasium doors and kept going.
The east gym doors. So you were right there by that entrance?
By the doors, yeah, but just walking. I didn't touch anything.
Okay. Let's talk about timing. Do you have any idea what time that would've been?
Honestly, no clue. Late, I guess.
Our cameras put someone at that entrance at about 11:40 p.m. Does that line up with when you walked through?
I couldn't tell you. I wasn't checking my phone.
The footage shows activity right around 11:40. Twenty to midnight. That mean anything to you?
I mean, twenty to midnight, sure, that could've been when I was cutting through. But that doesn't mean I did anything.
Fair enough. Now, the person on the footage is wearing something with a hood. A red hooded sweatshirt. Do you own one?
A red hoodie? No. I don't wear red, man. Never have.
You sure? Not even one in the back of a closet somewhere?
I'm telling you, that's not mine. I don't know anything about a red sweatshirt.
Alright. How'd you get to your cousin's that night? Did you drive?
I borrowed my roommate's car. Well, not borrowed exactly, he lets me use it.
What kind of car is that?
It's a little four-door. Dark colored, I think. I don't pay much attention to that stuff.
We've got a witness who saw a silver hatchback leaving that lot around the same time. Any chance that was you?
A silver hatchback? No, that's not the car I had. I don't know whose that is.
You're certain? Silver, hatchback, small.
I already said no. I can't help you with that one.
Let's go back to you walking through. Did you have both hands free? Carry anything?
Just the bag from the store. That's it.
I ask because the person on the footage has a mark on one hand. A cut on the left hand. You've got a bandage there yourself.
This? I got that moving furniture. Sliced it on a bracket. Nothing to do with anything.
So you'd say that cut has nothing to do with Friday night at the school?
Correct. I don't know anything about a cut on anybody's hand except my own.
Okay. Let me lay it out. We've got damage to a set of doors, we've got a time, and we've got a description. I'd like to clear this up tonight.
Then clear it up with somebody else, because I've told you everything I know.
One more time, from the top. Friday night. The store. The walk through the lot.
Same story as before. I bought what I bought, I walked where I walked, and I went home. That's it.
Alright, Mr. Halloran. I'm going to have you write all of that down for me, and we'll go from there.
